high.title: USD Falls and Closes Below R$ 4.90 for First Time Since January 2024
high.summary: The USD/BRL closed at R$ 4.8939 on Friday, falling 0.60% and marking the lowest level since January 15, 2024. The Brazilian real strengthened following strong U.S. employment data that reinforced expectations of higher U.S. interest rates for longer, and investor optimism about progress in Middle East peace negotiations. The dollar's weakness was broad-based, with the DXY index down 0.16% to 97.910 points. For the week, the dollar accumulated a 1.19% decline against the real. Markets continue monitoring geopolitical developments, particularly U.S.-Iran negotiations despite recent attacks between the two countries. This BRL strength is significant for international investors as it breaks through a key technical level and suggests potential for further real appreciation if global risk sentiment improves and Brazil maintains its monetary policy trajectory.

high.title: Lack of Clear Direction: COPOM Minutes Generate Divergent Market Readings and Keep IPCA+ 10.6% Annual Opportunities in Focus
high.summary: The Central Bank released COPOM meeting minutes detailing the decision to cut the Selic rate by 0.25 percentage points to 14.50% annually. However, the minutes generated divergent interpretations among investors regarding future monetary policy direction. Some market participants interpreted the tone as dovish, suggesting confidence in economic deceleration to sustain the cutting cycle. Others, including Empiricus Research's Lais Costa, viewed it as more hawkish. This uncertainty creates opportunities in inflation-linked bonds (IPCA+) yielding 10.6% annually, as markets remain unclear about the pace and extent of future rate cuts. The mixed signals are crucial for fixed income investors positioning for the next phase of Brazil's monetary cycle.

medium.title: Petrobras: Abreu e Lima Breaks Diesel Production Record in April
medium.summary: Petrobras' Abreu e Lima refinery in Pernambuco set a new diesel S-10 production record in April with 385 million liters, surpassing the previous record from 2016. The increase follows a capacity expansion project completed in 2025 that boosted refinery capacity to 130,000 barrels/day, resulting in approximately 60% higher diesel production compared to the same period last year. This operational improvement supports Petrobras' 2026-2030 business plan and helps mitigate impacts from global geopolitical tensions.

medium.title: New Desenrola: How High Interest Rates Pressure Family Debt?
medium.summary: Economists highlight that Brazil's elevated Selic rate combined with high banking spreads contributes to increased household debt, prompting the government to launch the "Novo Desenrola" program. Brazil's banking spread reached 34.6 percentage points in March, compared to a global average of around 6 p.p. according to the World Bank. The high Selic rate directly affects lending rates to families, pressuring household finances and economic activity.
